sentences.text:
Though served,
none appears for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4.
Perused the original record and proceedings.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2066/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined 3)

It is the case of the appellant that on 11.06.2016, the appellant was travelling in Chevrolet Spark car bearing No.GJ-07-CM-5520 and her husband was driven the said car in rash and negligent manner and when they reached near the place of accident, husband of the appellant lost control over the steering and dashed his car with the rickshaw bearing No.GJ-07-VV-7811, which was coming from opposite direction.
As a result, the appellant sustained grievous injuries including fracture.
Therefore, the appellant has filed MAC Petition seeking compensation.
After appreciating the evidence produced on record the learned Tribunal was pleased to partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- against the claim of Rs.7,00,000/-.

4) Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in considering the income of the injured as Rs.5,000/- p.m on notional basis as he was serving in medical store and used to earn Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Even considering the minimum wage prevailing at the time of accident, he has requested to reassess the income of the appellant.
Further, the Tribunal has erred in not considering future prospective income.
Also, the Tribunal has awarded meager amounts of Rs.30,000/- and Rs.10,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering and under the head of special diet and attendant charges respectively.
Hence, he has requested to enhance the compensation amount in the appeal.

5) Learned Advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavaty for respondent No.3 - Insurance Company has opposed the present appeal on the ground that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just, legal and proper and no interference is required to call for.
With these submissions he has requested to dismissed the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2066/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined 6)
Having considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and considering the material placed on record, it appears that the appeal is filed only on the aspect of quantum.

Hence,
this appeal is required to be decided on the aspect of quantum only.
Alleged incident is not in dispute.
Involvement of the vehicle is also not in dispute.

In order to prove the claim, Chief examination was produced at Exh:23, FIR at Exh:34, Panchnama of scene of incident at Exh:35,
Medical bills at Exhs:37 to 39, copy of injury certificates at Exh:31 and 32, disability certificate at Exhs:39 and 42 and medical bills at Exh:35.

7) As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC), that if no proof of income is produced on the record, then Tribunal has to consider prevalent minimum wages in absence of ample evidence of Minaben Karsanbhai Patel vs Karsanbhai Maganbhai Patel on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45796401/
2

In the present case, the accident occurred in June, 2016 and during that time, as per the Government approved minimum wages was Rs.7700/-, whereas, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the appellant as Rs.5,000/- per month, which required interference.

8) So far as disability is concerned, the appellant has produced a disability certificate at Exh:26 issued by Dr. Bhadresh Shah, wherein he has opined that the appellant sustained permanent partial impairment of 30 for the body as a whole.

The Tribunal relying on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of D. Sampath Vs. UII Com. Ltd, reported in 2011 ACJ 2466 and Rudra Vs. Divisional Manager, reported in 2011 (11) SCC 511, deposition of doctor and taking into consideration the fact there is always variation of plus minus 5% in the disablement assessed by the doctor, the Tribunal has assessed 25% partial permanent disablement of the appellant, which is not disputed by the parties.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2066/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined assessed 25% disability and this Court also deems fit not to disturb the aspect of disability.

9) In the present case, the accident occurred in June 2016 and during that time, the appellant - injured was serving in the medical store named Twisha Medical Store and was earning Rs.20,000/-
but she failed to produce any evidence to substantiate her income
. Therefore, as per the minimum wages fixed by the Government was Rs.7700/- for the year 2016.

As the Tribunal has considered multiplier of 7 as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. [2009 (6) SCC 121] which is also just and proper.

sentences.text: Now if we reassess the compensation with reassessed income of the injured Rs.7,700/- p.m income without adding any future loss of income as she was not entitled to get any future loss of income as she was 61 years old at the time of accident.

Therefore, by applying 7 multiplier and deduction of 25 %
disability
, it comes to Rs.1,61,700/- (Rs.7,700/- x 12 months x 7 multiplier x 25% disability) under the head of future loss of income.

10) As the Tribunal has already awarded Rs.1,05,000/- towards future loss of income, the appellant is entitled to get additional amount of Rs.56,700/- under the head of future loss of income.
11) So far as other amount awarded under other conventional heads are concerned, the same are just and proper and do not require any interference.
12)
So far actual loss of income for three months is concerned, the Tribunal has considering the monthly income of Rs.5,000/- p.m has awarded Rs.15,000/- for 3 months.

Here, this Court has reassessed the income of the injured as Rs.7,700/- p.m, therefore, the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2066/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined is entitled to get additional amount under the head of actual loss of income as Rs.8100/- (Rs.23,100/- - Rs.15,000/-).

13) As discussed above, the appellant is entitled to get compensation computed as under:
